newsitem.title: UK: Eurobourses mixed, jittery over inflation.
newsitem.headline: Eurobourses mixed, jittery over inflation.

text.p: European stocks put in a mixed performance on Wednesday, depressed by inflation pressures and ignoring Wall Street, which again set a record-breaking pace at the opening.
On currency markets, the dollar fell half a pfennig after the mark was buoyed up by a strong rise in an index of Germany's business climate, denting any hopes of an interest rate cut.
Frankfurt ended with a gain of 0.4 percent, outshining London and Paris which were down in mid-afternoon with investors worried over inflation.
German floor trade closed before New York's opening but had been boosted by the overnight showing on Wall Street, which saw its 40th record close of the year at 6,397.60 points.

But German stocks lost some of their gains after the jump in the October business confidence index of Germany's Ifo think-tank. Ifo's October survey showed a higher-than-expected jump in the business climate index last month to 97.4 percent from 95.7.
"The Ifo index was more or less stable but now there is a decent improvement," said one trader, adding that this had eroded hopes of a rate cut.
The figures pushed the computerised IBIS index, which measures after-hours deals, down by 0.7 percent in mid-afternoon.

London's FTSE index slipped 0.4 percent as investors were sent scurrying to the sidelines by stronger-than-expected October retail sales and money supply growth, which re-ignited fears of higher interest rates.
Dealers said they saw little scope for the British market to shake off its lethargy in the afternoon even though Wall Street touched a new intra-day peak of 6,438.59 points shortly after opening.
New York stocks jumped in early trading as investors ignored U.S. economic figures showing a big September trade gap but profit-takers later ate into some of the Wall Street's initial 40-point surge.
"We're not getting sucked in by Wall Street at the moment because we're so close to the budget...we need evidence of a tight budget to get us back on track," one dealer said.
"And the higher Wall Street goes, the more cautious we become of the correction that is bound to happen," he added.

The market, already anxious about prospects for the British budget on Tuesday, was alarmed after a 10.3 percent rise in M4 money supply, a big leap in bank and building society lending and the largest rise for two years in three-month figures for retail sales.
In Paris, French stocks gave up initial gains as bond prices fell on the German Ifo survey, which revived inflation worries.

The dollar weakened against the mark after the German business survey. "I am a bit surprised by the strength of this number. Hopes for a further rate cut (right now) will fade away," Guenter Redeker at Chase Manhattan in London said.
Earlier the Bundesbank said October annualised M3 money supply growth, its key monetary policy indicator, was unchanged at 8.4 percent from September.
"With the strong Ifo numbers and German M3 money supply, it does not look like there is room for a rate cut," said an economist at a Swiss bank.
CURRENCIES AT 1540 GMT
The dollar was quoted at 111.20 yen and 1.4977 marks, compared with 111.55 yen and 1.5036 marks in late European trade on Tuesday.
STOCK MARKETS AT 1540 GMT
LONDON - The Financial Times-Stock Exchange index of 100 leading British shares was down 16.8 points at 3,961.3.
PARIS - The CAC-40 share index was down 12.68 points at 2,227.37.
FRANKFURT - The 30-share DAX index closed up 10.41 points at 2,774.50.
PRECIOUS METALS
Gold fixed at $379.10 an ounce in the afternoon, compared to Tuesday's close of $378.45. Silver was stronger at $4.95, up five cents.
